name: TourEdge Pro 460cc
blurb: Adjustable loft, low-spin face and a genuinely forgiving 460cc head — the rare driver that suits a wide band of players.

name: Fairway Authority Max D
blurb: Heel-weighted draw bias with a deep centre of gravity. Built to straighten a slice without feeling like a corrective club.

name: Meridian TS Tour
blurb: A compact, low-spin head for players who shape shots on purpose. Punishing off the toe — that is the trade for the control.

name: Clubhouse Ascent 10.5
blurb: High-launch, lightweight build aimed at moderate swing speeds. The easiest club in this list to get airborne.

name: Vector CB Carbon
blurb: Carbon crown frees up weight for a wide, stable face. Long and forgiving, but the price only makes sense at speed.

name: Bunker Hill Stability 9
blurb: The widest effective face here. Mishits off the heel and toe lose distance slowly rather than falling off a cliff.

name: Augusta Line Fade Spec
blurb: Toe-weighted for players who fight a hook. A specialist club — wrong miss, wrong driver.

name: Clubhouse Origin Lite
blurb: The value pick. A light, high-launching head that does the job while a new player works out what they actually need.

name: Longbow XT Distance
blurb: Long, hot face built for chasing carry numbers. Rewards a centred strike and does little to help a bad one.

name: Greenkeeper Tempo 12°
blurb: Twelve degrees of loft and a soft, whippy profile for slower tempos. Built for height and a soft landing, not for distance.
